text:
[RFCS.10.3] The engine **must** emit a `ClockAdvance` event for every clock
value it observes, of either clock, under a live clock and a mock clock alike.
A value is observed when a sample reads it ([LTIM.2.8.4]); a mock clock's
value is observed by the next sample after it is set, not when it is set
([NTST.3.3]). It **must not** coalesce, decimate or omit the values its samples
observe.

A time-bound rule — `after:`, a TTL expiry, a `cooldown:` window — decides on
the value the engine held, so a value the trace does not carry is one a replay
cannot restore, and the rule fires somewhere the recording never was. Dropping
clock values to reduce trace size is sampling within a kind, which
[LFST.12.8] forbids, and the saving is bought from the guarantee
([LFST.1.3]).
